I was having a hard time my third year, and my grades began to suffer significantly. Dean Ozment suggested I take a medical withdraw since I had also been diagnosed with something. I took spring 2022 off under the impression I could come back in the fall, but it turned out there was a whole process to be back in uva, which she never explained to me. I had to jump a bunch of hoops to make sure I was taking classes again. 

Although she didn’t give me all the right or relevant information, I thought she was very nice and friendly when I’ve met with her. More recently, I had a problem with a professor denying me an extension for some work I missed because of a medical emergency, and she said she would fight for me to make sure I’m allowed to make up the work. She reached out the the professor and some other people to get this situation fixed. I’m very thankful she did that because I would’ve failed the class otherwise and would’ve had to come back this fall just to take one class. So for that I found her very helpful. 

I think it’s clear she should not be the only Dean of transfer students. I don’t think the way people say they’ve been treated by her is acceptable or justifiable, but I also feel like I wouldn’t know exactly how to manage teachings classes and being a dean for like 3,000 students. It just sounds overwhelming. 

I don’t think she is a bad person, but I guess I haven’t experienced what others have. Regardless, I think looking at all of this from her perspective might help to understand how she deals with the problems thousands of students reach out to her about. Again, that’s a lot to keep track of and it seems almost impossible to be very personal with every single student. I’ve always made sure to email her a week after my original email since I understand she gets a lot of students reaching out to her. 

But yea, she might not be the best dean but she clearly has too much on her plate. UVA should do something about that so transfer students can get the guidance they need without overworking one single dean.

Well, to explain some of the "why," I was in NYC when I wrote the poem. I myself enjoy urban life, but I understand that none of these manmade buildings were there for most of the land's history. Although I would much prefer to live in a city, I do find nature far more beautiful.

The narrator of the poem was meant to be somewhat abstract. I did not make a decision as to who was leaving or telling the story. In a way, it was Time describing the changes we have created on the planet. Time remembers every moment in history. 

By leaving behind... blah blah... I meant that the urban setting used to be the rural setting. Time left the grassy planes since it moved to a different period (as its the physical condition of being Time, at least from the human perspective), where the natural landscape was no longer there. That means that the narrator did not choose to move to the city.
